thread:
ashley: Customer reported duplicate outgoing invites + double billing after model triggered our send_invite tool. Happened ~30s apart. They attached traces.
ashley: Logs look like service returned 202 then we retried and it executed again. No idempotency-key present in client calls.
sam: Can you paste the request/response headers from the interaction? Particularly X-Request-ID and the toolcall payload.
ashley: paste below (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/call_tool send_invite
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
X-Request-ID: 01F8Z9Y2

body: {"user_email":"cc@customer.com","name":"CC","action":"invite"}
```
Response 1: 202 Accepted, body: {"status":"queued","call_id":"c-123"}
Response 2 (retry): 200 OK, body: {"status":"ok","invite_id":"i-789"}
ashley: The client says it retried after no final confirmation from our side. Our runtime turning fallbacks on might have caused a second execution.
kai: Did the function call include a schema for args? If args failed validation we usually fallback to plain tool invocation. Could that have created two distinct execution paths?
sam: Good point — I see in the tool metadata the tool expects args: {"email": "string", "meta": {"ref":"string"}} but model sent {"user_email":...}. That triggers schema-mismatch handling which attempts a best-effort conversion and then falls back to non-tool (text) path, which our router can then re-invoke tool.
ashley: So flow might be: 1) initial function_call -> schema validation error -> router fallback to non-tool (model text) -> runtime sees no completion -> client retries -> second invocation executes tool. Duplicate side-effect.
sam: Repro steps to validate: 1) Send function_call with mismatched arg name (user_email). 2) Block idempotency header. 3) Observe 202 then 200 and duplicate effect.
kai: Short-term mitigation: enforce stricter schema validation (reject and return 4xx) or ensure tool execution is idempotent by requiring idempotency-key on tool invocation. We should also make fallback logic avoid re-invoking tool when schema mismatch is the cause.
ashley: Customer asked for refund for duplicate charge; billing-bot did auto-refund but wants incident so we can patch.
sam: Assigning: @kai to produce a small fix for schema path and @ashley to own customer comms. I'll open a follow-up thread with CI repro. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 - toolcall-fallback-dup-exec. Priority: P2.
billing-bot: Refund of $12.00 issued to cc@customer.com. Reference RB-4456.
ashley: I'll attach a minimal repro curl in the incident. Thanks everyone.
